output.name: Minta

anatomy.part: brim centre where the crown sits

output.myth: A fisherman had a hat his mother sewed from the last good sailcloth, and he wore it to the boats every morning, because a hat is a thing a man can count on. Tavo saw it from the bay one windy day and laughed so hard he nearly fell out of the sky. He came down, took the hat off the man's head as neatly as a child takes a biscuit, and sailed it up past the reach of any hand. The man shouted. Aun, who was idling on the cliff with his own kite, said that a Gale who laughs will not give back a hat. Tavo cannot be bargained with, so the fisherman tried Hesk instead, and she only wound her string and said the hat was not in her count. Now the hat hangs in Vel with its ribbon trailing down toward the bay. On calm nights the fishermen look up and say it is the only hat in Vel that will never be wet.
output.verse:
Tavo laughed, and took
his hat sailed past every hand
its ribbon trails down
